<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 20c7073bc392c5fbb3817f2eab03b88bbe5f0739` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `80081402797ec4a9a65b60e7c0c02e32bedb1279` — the merge of head `649d7ef505917cadc2a589ad0d3e43da01f3e10b` into base `20c7073bc392c5fbb3817f2eab03b88bbe5f0739`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 80081402797ec4a9a65b60e7c0c02e32bedb1279 && git checkout 80081402797ec4a9a65b60e7c0c02e32bedb1279
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 20c7073bc392c5fbb3817f2eab03b88bbe5f0739 649d7ef505917cadc2a589ad0d3e43da01f3e10b && git checkout -B drift-repro 20c7073bc392c5fbb3817f2eab03b88bbe5f0739 && git merge --no-ff 649d7ef505917cadc2a589ad0d3e43da01f3e10b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 20c7073bc392c5fbb3817f2eab03b88bbe5f0739
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9e46bbcc9706941301222dedb85fbd4b3c3fd21e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-filter.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-having-comparand-shape.test.ts, and the two implementing files packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts (`assertFilterNodeShapes`), packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts (its two call sites) + read, not reviewed: packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/filter-refusal.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-verdict.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (`isWhereFilterObject`)

Face: narrowing. Inputs: card #32123 and its six comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (5 files, +259 −1), and the 60 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run; every statement about behaviour below is read from the tree at the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- `aggregations[i].filter`, accept-set narrowed: a `$and` / `$or` element or a `$not` operand that is not a plain object (literal or null-prototype), and a `$and` / `$or` that is not an array, now answer `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Right: `FilterConditionSchema` on `main` declares `$and` / `$or` as `FilterCondition[]` and `$not` as `FilterCondition`, so no spec-valid filter is in the refused set, and each refused shape was read by the walker (`matchesHaving`) as no constraint, as index-named columns or as a one-element list.
- `having`, the same narrowing at the same gate. Right, and inside the surface: claim amendment 6770129950 widens the file surface to `having` and records the four in-place conditions.
- The non-list `$and` / `$or` half. Right: every driver gate refuses it on `where` (`filterNodeListExpectedError`, `assertFilterNodeList`), and the spec's reduction hands a non-array to exactly that hook. `undefined` as the operand is refused too, as it is on `where`.
- Object-form accept-set unchanged. Right, read against the predicate: the gate throws only on a non-array combinator or a non-plain-object node, descends only `$and` / `$or` / `$not` at node positions (the walker's own positions), never descends a field constraint (so an array comparand under `$in` or a field-level operator map is untouched), accepts `$and: []` / `$or: []`, and accepts null-prototype nodes. Its node predicate is byte-for-byte the drivers' `isFilterNode`. The suite's seven filter controls and four `having` controls pin this.
- Public surface: none. `assertFilterNodeShapes` is exported from the module only; `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` does not re-export `having-filter.ts` members by that name and the package exposes `.` and `./core` alone. No schema, no error code and no option key is added.
- Envelope: `invalidFilterError` (`code` `INVALID_FILTER`, `status` 400, `httpStatus` 400), the envelope the neighbouring doors at both positions already speak. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. It matches what the diff publishes: one package, no added surface, a refusal where a wrong figure was answered. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: holds. The refused operands are outside `FilterConditionSchema`, so no stored, schema-validated row changes shape and there is nothing to migrate.
- Gate verdicts on the head: `Check Changeset` success (the newest run; one earlier run was cancelled by the body patch and superseded), `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core (1/8 … 8/8)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards` all success. No check-run on the head concluded failure.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (`$nor` words and position): answered in part, escalated in part. In code, status and timing the card's rule holds (the key is refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 before any read, its operand never counted, now pinned). The words are the walker's, not `where`'s, and the position is the clause, not `.$nor`. The PR body says this was "left as is by the seat's ruling", but no comment on #32123 records that ruling. See ④ finding 1.
- Open question 2 (repo-wide `pnpm lint`): answered by the head's check-runs, `Lint · ESLint` and the lint gate families success.
- Open question 3 (who patches the PR body): answered. The body at this head carries the narrowing arm, the `Skills-docs:` line and the disposition sentence.
- Deviation, `having` and the non-list half: answered by claim amendment 6770129950.
- Deviation, second changeset commit for the ADR-0087 marker: answered, `Check Changeset` success.
- Deviations on scratch files and the commit trailer: process notes, no effect on the tree.
- Out-of-scope finding, the plugin-driver `where` floor (`applyDriverQueryInMemory` answers the same four shapes): escalated to the lane seat. The thread names no card for it, and it is the same wrong-figure class one verb over. It is not this PR's to fix (outside the claimed surface).
- Out-of-scope note, no shared home for the node-shape text: noted, a refactor; no action owed here.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the card, sentence by sentence:

- "refused with `INVALID_FILTER` in the words the same operand gets in `where`": holds for `$and` / `$or` / `$not`. Both constructors are byte-identical to `driver-memory`'s `filterNodeExpectedError` / `filterNodeListExpectedError`, including the `kind (preview)` rendering (`describeFlagOperand` equals `describeFilterOperand` plus `safeShapePreview`, 80-character cut included), and identical to `driver-sql`'s full diagnostic (its author-marked wire text; a withheld `where` refusal on driver-sql is the generic sentence instead). `driver-mongodb` differs by one word (finding 3).
- "It is never evaluated and counted" and "before any row is read, on every driver": holds. Both calls sit before `getDriver` (line 1210 at the head), so neither `driver.aggregate` nor the in-memory fallback is reached; the tests assert zero `find` / `aggregate` calls on a native-capable and a raw driver.
- "with the position named (`aggregations[i].filter.$and[0]`)": holds, and the index pin covers `aggregations[2]`.
- First at each position: holds for the doors that walk a node. On the per-aggregation `filter` the gate follows only the whole-filter object check and precedes `assertListComparandShapes` and every later door; on `having` it follows only `assertHavingIsFilterCondition`. The two guards earlier in the verb (`rejectInternalFieldEvaluation`, `rejectCredentialEvaluation`) also read these filters; they refuse or pass and cannot answer a figure, and the suite shows they do not throw an uncoded error on a `null` or string element.
- "Tests: one per combinator, object-form controls unchanged, an empty table and a populated table answer alike; ablation red": holds for `$and`, `$or`, `$not`; `$nor` is pinned as the pre-existing unknown-operator refusal. `Test Core` is green on the head; the ablation readings are the dev's (12 and 7 red), not re-run here by rule.
- The narrowing against the published spec: it makes the spec's own declaration real at two positions and takes no declared capability away.

Attempts to break it, all read from the code: a null-prototype node (accepted); nested combinators (descended, position path correct); `$in` with an array and other array comparands (not descended); `$and: []` and `$or: []` (accepted, identities unchanged); `$and: undefined` (refused, as on `where`); a `Date`, `Map` or class-instance element (refused, as on `where`); a field-level `$not` inside an operator map (not a node position, untouched).

Findings:

1. should-fix — `$nor`: the card's Rule names `$nor` and asks for `where`'s words. The head refuses it in the walker's words (`Unsupported operator '$nor' in ...`) at the clause root, while `where` says `Unsupported filter combinator "$nor" at where.$nor`. The defect the card measures (a counted wrong figure) does not exist for `$nor`, so this does not block; but the deviation from the Rule's text is recorded only in the PR body. The seat should record the ruling on #32123, or file the follow-up the dev recommended (option B).
2. should-fix — a filter root that is a class instance. The per-aggregation root test is `isWhereFilterObject` (`Object.prototype.toString` gives `[object Object]`, which a class instance passes), and `assertFilterNodeShapes` opens with `if (!isPlainFilterNode(filter)) return`. So an in-process `aggregations[i].filter` that is a class instance carrying `$and: [[...]]` passes the root check, skips the new gate and is still walked by `matchesHaving`, which takes any object. Read from the code, not run. It is reachable only in-process (the wire door parses the schema), it mirrors the same early return in `driver-memory`'s gate, and `having` is not affected (its root check requires a plain prototype). Closing it is one line: walk the root unconditionally, since the caller has already judged it. Non-blocking.
3. nit — the JSDoc of `assertFilterNodeShapes` says all three drivers refuse "in the same words". `driver-mongodb`'s node refusal ends "which documents match", not "which rows match". The code comment further down ("a declared verbatim copy of `driver-memory`'s ... = `driver-sql`'s author-facing text") is the accurate one.
4. nit — when one filter is malformed twice, the first refusal can differ from `where`'s: the drivers judge unknown `$` keys and field constraints in the same walk as node shapes, while here the shape gate runs whole before the walker. Either way the answer is `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 before any read.
5. nit — the `having` suite has no `$not: null` row, no non-list `$and` row and no null-prototype control; the per-aggregation suite has all three and both positions call one function.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 are for the lane seat to carry; neither changes what this narrowing refuses or answers for a spec-valid filter.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32123-aggregate-filter-combinator`
Reviewed-by: `session_01J8VVAnTcb4cZVkPdhkPicW`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1636b8c6fed6519b93e1aa9a5d4f76f539879ef0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-filter.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-having-comparand-shape.test.ts, and the two implementing files packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts (`assertFilterNodeShapes`), packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts (its two call sites) + read, not reviewed: packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/filter-refusal.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-verdict.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (`isWhereFilterObject`)

Delta review. This record supersedes 6783337415 (head `9e46bbcc`). Face: narrowing. Inputs: the one commit `9e46bbcc..1636b8c6` (3 files, +45 −3: `having-filter.ts` and the two suites), the two new comments on #32123 (seat ruling 6783358330, dev report 6784377562), the PR body, and the check-runs on the new head. The rest of the diff against `main` is unchanged from the reviewed head and its judgments stand. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- The gate's root test changes from "a plain object" to "any non-null, non-array object". Right. Only two callers exist: the per-aggregation call, whose root has passed `isWhereFilterObject`, and the `having` call, whose root is absent or already plain. So the only root newly walked is a class-instance per-aggregation filter, and the only thing newly refused is such a root carrying a malformed combinator operand, which was read as a wrong figure before.
- Below the root nothing moves: elements and the `$not` operand are still held to the drivers' plain-object predicate, and the recursion only ever receives a node that passed it.
- Object-form accept-set: unchanged. A class-instance root with a valid filter is walked and passes; the new control pins that it counts what its literal twin counts (3 of 6) on both driver kinds.
- Public surface: none, as before. No changeset or engine file is touched by the delta.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the changeset and the PR body, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The delta widens the narrowing only to an in-process shape outside `FilterConditionSchema`, so the level and the disposition still match.
- Check-runs on the new head: 55 in all, none failed. `Test Core (1/8 … 8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint · ESLint`, the lint gate families, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards` are success. `Check Changeset` has one run success and one still in progress at the time of this record (pending; the changeset file is unchanged by this commit). The rest are skipped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `$nor` (earlier finding 1): closed. Seat ruling 6783358330 is now on the card: `$nor` is not in the spec's `LOGICAL_OPERATORS`, the refusal stands in the walker's words, no card.
- Plugin-driver `where` floor (escalated in the earlier record): closed, filed as #32252 per the same comment.
- New out-of-scope finding in report 6784377562, driver-memory's own `where` gate skipping a class-instance root: the brief for this round states it was added to #32252 as a second position. That placement is not visible on #32123's thread, so the seat should confirm it there. Not this PR's surface.
- The dev report carries no open question and no new deviation this round.

### ④ Design judgment

- Is refusing the class-instance root right against the card's Rule? Yes. The Rule's first sentence is "a filter is answered one way at every position on a verb", and its defect is a filter "evaluated and counted". At this position the engine accepts a class-instance root and the walker reads it as a node, so the same content must get the literal's answer: refused when the operand is malformed, counted when it is valid. Matching driver-memory's `where` here would have meant copying its early return, which by the dev's measurement answers `[]` or an uncoded `TypeError`. The engine now holds the Rule's answer and the driver's gap is carried separately.
- Position and words for the new refusal are the literal's (`aggregations[1].filter.$and[0]`), pinned by the new row through the same helper as the others (code, status, zero reads, empty and populated).
- Tried against the new root test: `null`, `undefined`, a string and an array root return without a walk, as before (the callers refuse or skip those earlier); a `Map` or `Date` never reaches the gate at either position; a getter-backed or inherited `$and` is not an own enumerable key, and the walker uses the same `Object.entries` read, so the gate and the walker see one key set.

Earlier findings:

1. should-fix (`$nor`) — closed by the ruling on the card.
2. should-fix (class-instance root) — closed by this commit; read in `assertFilterNodeShapes` and pinned by a refusal row and a control.
3. nit (JSDoc words) — closed; the JSDoc now names driver-mongodb's one-word difference.
4. nit (first refusal on a doubly malformed filter can differ from `where`'s) — carried over, unchanged, no action owed.
5. nit (`having` rows) — closed; `$not: null`, a non-list `$and` and a null-prototype control are added.

New findings: none.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32123-aggregate-filter-combinator`
Reviewed-by: `session_01J8VVAnTcb4cZVkPdhkPicW`

**VERDICT: PASS**
